title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One day lost in a 7-day week; store closed for renovation. No prior closure data, but similar impact from holidays (e.g., Labor Day: 54 units vs 44.4 baseline) suggests ~14% lift loss.

drivers.name: Price increase (+2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior price hikes at $6.56: sales were 24 and 53, both near or below baseline. Noise-adjusted estimate shows no lift. No past promotion at this price point.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 44.4. The target week has a price increase to $6.56 (+2.3%), with a store closure on Monday (reducing sales days). No event or promotion is scheduled. Past price increases (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw no lift; in fact, sales dipped to 24 and 53, respectively. The noise-adjusted price effect is near 1.0. The store closure reduces expected sales days by 1/7 (~14.3%), but the baseline already accounts for seasonal trends. No promotion or event drives uplift. The classical model suggests no change, and evidence supports this. Confidence is medium due to sparse price-effect data.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.4 | 5%-95%: 14.3 - 72.8 | 10%-90%: 22.3 - 68.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
